page: OVHcloud b3-64 is a general-purpose cloud server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations show strong performance in memory operations and single-core CPU tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in large-block memory read and write bandwidth tests, as well as in Passmark memory scoring and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core CPU performance, static web serving throughput, and database operations fall within the average range. The absence of hyperthreading means each of the 16 vCPUs maps directly to a physical core, which ensures consistent compute allocation but limits parallel thread density compared to hyperthreaded alternatives.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and integrated NVMe storage offer a predictable resource profile without the risk of noisy-neighbor CPU degradation. This balance of dedicated compute, high memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage makes the b3-64 well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, text processing, and medium-scale database hosting.
description: The OVHcloud b3-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 threads, running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates strong performance in single-core CPU tasks, large-block memory read/write bandwidth, and multi-threaded decompression, while multi-core CPU and database operations perform at average levels. Lacking hyperthreading, the instance provides dedicated, non-shared physical cores, ensuring stable compute performance. This hardware profile is highly suitable for software compilation, text processing, medium-scale databases, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring consistent CPU and memory throughput.
